candidate.note: A planet candidate from an automated search, not a confirmed planet. It needs review by people and follow-up observations; other things, such as a faint background binary, can look the same.

checks.name: snr
checks.reason: The dip stands 30 times above the noise over 24 events.

checks.name: odd_even
checks.reason: Alternate dips have matching depths (0.117% vs 0.126%), as expected for a planet.

checks.name: secondary_eclipse
checks.reason: Halfway round the orbit there is no significant dip, consistent with a planet.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: Dip depth 0.122% on a 0.68 R_sun star implies about 0.23 Jupiter radii (2.6 Earth radii), likely range 0.21-0.25. That is within the size range of planets.

checks.name: period_alias
checks.reason: The period holds up against P/2, 2P and 3P: P/2: dip at half phase 1% of the main one; 2P: shallowest group 90% of the rest; 3P: shallowest group 88% of the rest.

checks.name: momentum_dump
checks.reason: 1 of 24 dips coincide with a momentum dump and 0 more with quality-flagged cadences; the clean dips alone are 100% as deep as all of them, so the signal does not come from spacecraft events.

checks.name: sector_depth
checks.reason: The dip depth agrees between sectors (S63 1219±79, S90 1126±78, S100 1196±76 ppm; chance of this scatter 0.68).

checks.name: duration
checks.reason: The dip lasts 1.6 h; a planet crossing the middle of this star (density 2.13 solar, from TIC density) on a 3.283-day orbit would take about 2.2 h, so the length fits.

checks.name: single_sector
checks.reason: Not a single-sector signal: dips were seen in 3 sectors.

score_detail.formula: (0.40*S_snr + 0.20*S_transits + 0.25*S_checks + 0.15*S_brightness) * (0.8 if single-sector); each part = weight * S * factor
